reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's a Wednesday in August. Nothing special about it. No milestone, no crisis, no chip to pick up. Just a middle-of-the-week day in the middle of a summer that will end whether you're paying attention or not.

When I was drinking, Wednesdays didn't exist. They were just the thing between Tuesday's hangover and Thursday's pre-game. The whole middle of my life was scaffolding for the weekend, and the weekend was scaffolding for forgetting. Sobriety gave me Wednesdays back. That sounds small until you realize a life is mostly Wednesdays. It's not the summit day of the ski trip or the wedding or the promotion — it's the coffee before work, the walk after dinner, the text to a friend that you actually remember sending. That's where the life lives.

Durant's line about Aristotle gets quoted so much it's almost wallpaper, but it's true in a way that matters here. You don't become a person you can live with in one heroic swing. You become that person on Wednesdays. In the small unglamorous choice to make the bed, call your sponsor, go to the meeting, eat a real meal, get some sleep. The days you'll never remember are the ones building the person you're becoming. Show up for this one.
reflection.meditation: What is one small, ordinary thing I can do well today — not because it's dramatic, but because it's mine?

affirmations: I am building my life in the ordinary hours, not just the big ones.
Today I get to be present for a day I would have slept through before.
I am capable of showing up for small things, and small things are what a life is made of.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a plain Wednesday I actually get to be inside of. Grateful for the version of me that white-knuckled through early days so this one could feel this normal. Grateful for coffee that tastes like coffee, for a clear head at 3pm, for friends whose numbers I can call without shame. None of this was on the menu when I was drinking.
gratitude.closing: One more ordinary day. That's the whole gift.
